notes: The page continues an étale-local construction of a map between the displayed higher direct images and hence between their H^1(S, ) groups. The unidentified left coefficient prevents a fully semantic identification of that object from this page alone.

It specializes to a relative curve C with m prime = 2 and the class of the difference of two section divisors. The source says connected geometric fibres make x prime primitive, and allows any relative divisor of relative degree zero.

It then takes Z to be a codimension-n algebraic cycle on the printed product Y x_S C, writes its degree-2n class with twist n, and gives x as the class of z = Z(t_1) - Z(t_o), with o/0 an index-label reading uncertainty.

The author explicitly qualifies the construction: “pour que cette classe de cohomologie soit vraiment définie en l’état actuel de la Science, il faut faire des hypothèses restrictives”. The listed alternatives are finite type over a field, excellent of the clipped characteristic nulle, or a relative cycle with the visible fibrewise inequality ≤ n.

The final reservation says “on suppose que les intersections écrites ont un sens”, or that classes of cycles are used so the intersections have a meaning; the latter is again qualified by finite type over a field. Neither long NB receives an added closing parenthesis.
The fibrewise codimension sign was checked visually rather than reversed on mathematical grounds. Its slanted lower rule is leqslant. The page does not itself prove adequacy of the listed hypotheses.

The apparent degree-zero argument motivates a limited conditional arithmetic check only. Primitivity, existence of cycle classes, correspondence functoriality, and the asserted intersection construction were transcribed, not proved here.

The first coefficient has overlapping contours but no securely ordered deletion/insertion layers. It is retained as one uncertain glyph, with ordinary E first; the heavier impression is not enough to assert a double-struck alphabet.
The isolated right-edge diagonal and pale lower-edge traces have no secure textual attachment. They are documented without inventing authorial letters or drawings.
Missing H handwriting wrappers alone were not counted as differences. Rule provenance is recorded in the inventory; an underline does not relabel the underlying typed word as handwriting.

check_events.outcome: Conditional arithmetic computation, no formal certificate: assuming each section restricts to a rational point of degree one on the relevant geometric curve fibre and divisor degree is defined, deg(t_1(S)-t_o(S)) = 1 - 1 = 0 on that fibre. This checks the degree subtraction only; it does not prove the primitive-class assertion, nor existence/compatibility of cycle classes or intersections.

brief_feedback: The v02 distinction between literal glyph reading and missing handwriting wrappers is useful. A further clarification would help for (i) a typewriter lowercase-o-shaped glyph serving as zero, (ii) a possible paragraph boundary with no blank or indent, and (iii) an isolated edge trace that is visible but not securely authorial. R1 records these limits rather than normalizing them. No extra crop or repeat whole/half view was needed.
